# Recipe — judge a Visual Contract against a real capture

A spec that renders something a person looks at carries a `## Visual Contract`: numbered rows, each
settleable by **looking at one capture**. This recipe is the command that settles them.

It exists because the alternative was measured and is worse. On one SKU, a rung built from nine
hand-found sample-point coordinates cost **62 minutes and $18.46 of a single story run** — 30 one-off
pixel probes interleaved with 12 re-captures, just to *discover* the coordinates — and then certified
two real defects as correct: goods rendering visibly unattached to the shelf, and a `+N` badge whose
label broke out of its fill. Both passed every field assertion, the mutation fixtures and four review
layers. Nine points only ever check the nine things somebody thought to sample; one pass over the
whole capture found both in 23 seconds.

## What it is for, and what it is not for

| Use it to settle | Do **not** use it to settle |
|---|---|
| Is the ground deliberate, or is the rig default reaching the player? | An exact scale — `0.72` against `0.80` |
| Does a container draw its empty slots, or is it a bare panel? | An exact colour value |
| Do objects read as resting on a surface rather than floating? | A `sortingOrder`, a 9-slice mode, a `spriteDrawMode` |
| Does a label sit inside its fill and stay legible? | Anything whose truth is a number the eye cannot read |
| Does the surface read as finished rather than as a wireframe? | Whether a *suite* passed |

Everything in the right-hand column is a **field assertion** in the spec's `## Tasks & Acceptance`.
The judge returning `CANNOT-TELL` on a row is the signal to write one — that is how the parameter
checks get *derived* instead of invented.

## Install

Nothing to install. The script is **shipped by the framework** and lands at `Tools/pf/visual-judge.sh`,
executable, whenever the agent-doc sync runs:

```sh
Tools/Build/pf-build.sh agentdocs          # or Framework/Agent Docs/Sync in the editor
Tools/Build/pf-build.sh agentdocs --check  # gate: exit 1 names any tool missing, stale or not +x
```

It is a generated file — edit it in the framework repo (`Documentation~/agent/tools/`), never in the
SKU. `Tools/UiGate/` stays yours: the contracts, the references, the captures, the calibration note.

The captures it judges are produced by the framework capture harness — **Framework/UiGate/Run All
Capture Fixtures**, or `CaptureHarness.Run(CaptureHarness.FixturePath("<fixture>"))` from an EditMode
test or MCP `script-execute` — at `Tools/UiGate/captures/<fixture>.png`. The SKU supplies one
`ICaptureProject` and a `CaptureSurface<T>` per surface; see the `pf-uigate` skill, "The capture
harness".

It shells out to an external agent CLI that accepts images — `codex exec`. Two mechanics that cost
real time to discover, if you ever port it:

- `-i/--image` is **variadic**, so a positional prompt is swallowed as another image path. The prompt
  goes on **stdin** and the argument list ends with `-`.
- Pass `--ignore-user-config` so the judge does not inherit the repo's own agent hooks.
- **Shrink the upload, not the image.** Nine 768 px PNGs are 8.3 MB on the wire, and a call took
  398–860 s. The same pixels as JPEG q90 4:4:4 are 2.1 MB, and a call took 63–76 s, with identical
  token counts. Callers' caps killed the slow calls, and those kills read as a dead transport.

## Exit-code contract

The usual `0` Ok · `1` Drift · `2` Error, plus `3`: `0` = no row VIOLATED, `1` = at least one, `2` =
the judge could not run **or the capture is flat and therefore broken**, `3` = HALT, the same row has
been VIOLATED twice against a byte-identical capture. **A judge that did not run is never a pass** —
exit `2` is a finding, and exit `3` means stop coding and re-read the row.

Run the deterministic floor first: `Tools/pf/pixel-probe.py`. Full procedure: the `pf-uigate` skill.

## The script

`Tools/pf/visual-judge.sh` — read its header for the full flag list. Four things it does **before**
it will spend a model call, each of which has burned a real loop:

1. **Broken-capture check**, on every capture. A near-flat frame did not render; that is a
   capture-pipeline fault, not a UI fault. Exit `2` naming the file and the measured luma variance —
   never `1`, and never a VIOLATED row, because every row would come back VIOLATED naming the wrong
   cause.
2. **HALT check.** The archive is read back first. Same row VIOLATED in each of the last two runs and
   these captures byte-identical to the last? The model has nothing new to look at. Exit `3`.
3. **Cache.** The whole input — prompt, every image's bytes, model, effort, encoding, sample count —
   is hashed. An input already judged returns its archived verdict with no model call, so
   re-judging the stage's final capture at audit and at review costs nothing. The verdict it
   returns is a replay, and the model is not deterministic (next section). Keep
   `UIGATE_JUDGE_SAMPLES` above 1 so the replay is of a settled verdict.
4. **Archive.** Every run lands in `Tools/UiGate/captures/<surface>/<stamp>-<verdict>.{png,md}` — the
   captures as judged, the caller, the model and effort, every image with its hash, the V-lines, the
   wall time, the tokens, and the hash of the contract that produced them.

**Hand the judge every image a row compares against.** A row that asks whether a panel matches
another surface's family, or whether finish is comparable to a benchmark, is unanswerable unless that
second image is attached. The contract carries them in a fenced ` ```visual-judge ` block (`root:`,
`reference: path | label`, `capture: path | label`, `notes: file#section`); run
`visual-judge.sh --spec <spec>` and every call site judges the same inputs. References are attached
first and the prompt numbers every image, so each verdict names the capture and the reference it
read. Pass `--dry-run` to print the prompt and the exact `codex` argv without spending a call.

**Pin the model** in the SKU's `Tools/UiGate/judge.conf` (`VISUAL_JUDGE_MODEL=`,
`VISUAL_JUDGE_EFFORT=`). `--ignore-user-config` keeps the repo's agent hooks away from the judge, and
it also drops the user's configured model — unpinned, the judge runs the CLI's built-in default.

## Bounding the loop

Three rules, or this becomes the loop it replaced:

- **The judge's `LOOP:` line decides when to stop**, not the caller's count. Each verdict ends with
  `LOOP: round n/N · … · continue | stop (…) | done`, under the SKU's policy in `judge.conf`:
  `UIGATE_LOOP_POLICY=fixed` stops after `UIGATE_LOOP_MAX_ROUNDS` rounds (default 3); `progress`
  continues while every round leaves fewer rows VIOLATED and stops at the first round that does not,
  or at the ceiling. A row still VIOLATED at `stop` is reported open, not iterated on.
- **Only judge a capture that changed.** Re-judging an identical capture buys no new round: the judge
  answers it from its cache. That is a policy, not a property of the model. Measured 2026-09-23, a
  byte-identical input judged all-SATISFIED in the morning came back with three rows VIOLATED in
  3 of 3 re-runs that evening. So a verdict is worth caching only when it has been reproduced.
  `UIGATE_JUDGE_SAMPLES=K` makes the judge count a row only when K independent calls agree (it
  starts with K calls in parallel and adds calls up to 2K-1 for split rows). A row that never gets
  K agreeing votes is reported `VIOLATED — unsettled`.
- **Let the judge own its clock.** One ceiling, `UIGATE_JUDGE_TIMEOUT` (default 840 s, under the
  host's 15-minute Bash cap), covers every model call in a run. Never wrap the judge in a shorter
  cap.
- **One round, one fix pass** — fix every VIOLATED row the round returned before re-capturing, exactly
  as with a red test run.

## Before you let it block anything

Its catch rate is a number, not a belief. Run the surface's mutation fixtures past it and require it
to catch each one while passing the clean capture; record the rate **with the model identity that
produced it**, and re-measure when the model or the prompt changes. Until that number exists, treat
its output as findings for triage rather than a unilateral block.
